chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Jahm ibn Humeyd, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do you not take protection of their Sultan (ruling authorities)?' I said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why (not)?' I said, 'My Religion would flee from me'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So are you determined upon that?' I said, 'Yes'. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Now, your Religion is safe for you'.

key_terms.تَغْشَى: To take protection or seek refuge with
key_terms.سَلِمَ لَكَ دِينُكَ: Your religion is safe for you
key_terms.فِرَاراً بِدِينِي: My religion fleeing; fear of religious compromise

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of not seeking protection from ruling authorities for the safety of one's religion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates Jahm ibn Humayd’s strategy of avoiding political submission to the Umayyad caliphs, interpreting his refusal to seek protection as an act of preserving religious integrity. This narrative is central to the Shia doctrine of *al-Bara’ah* (disassociation) from unjust rulers, illustrating that steadfastness in faith often requires distancing oneself from the mechanisms of temporal power. The Imam’s declaration confirms that such deliberate avoidance is not mere cowardice but a successful preservation of one's spiritual standing.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Jahm Bin Humeyd who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Do you not take protection of their Sultan (ruling authorities)?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And why (not)?’ I said, ‘My Religion would flee from me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So are you determined upon that?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Now, your Religion is safe for you’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Jahm ibn Humayd who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘Do you use the power of these people for cover?’ I replied, ‘No, I do not do so.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Why do you not do so?’ I replied, ‘It is because of my running away with my religion.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Are you determined in this issue?’ I replied, ‘Yes, I am determined.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Now your religion is safe for you.’”
